overview: White plays Nc3, d3 and g3, setting up a King's Indian Attack-style fianchetto while Black has taken space with d5 and Nf6. White continues Bg2, e4 and Nf3 or Nge2, keeping the structure flexible. Neither side has forced play and the game is positional.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, then play e4
Develop Nf3 and castle, keeping the centre flexible

typical_structures.structure: Reversed King's Indian or reversed Pirc with d3/e4
Closed or semi-open centre with tension on e4

character.notes: Slow set-up play with little tactical risk for either side.

soundness.notes: The set-up is sound and low-risk, if unambitious.

structure.notes: Neither side has committed the centre; it can become a KID reversed or a flexible centre.

approach.notes: Set-up of Nc3, d3, g3, Bg2 that can be played against most replies.

level.notes: The plan is easy to follow but moves have to be accurate to get an edge.

sublines_that_differ.name: Van Geet Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: an earlier e4 and a sharper structure

character.reason: The set-up is quiet and hard to lose quickly.

soundness.reason: The line is a safe, unambitious set-up.

approach.reason: White plays the same Nc3/d3/g3/Bg2 plan against almost anything.

level.reason: The plans are clear but the move order needs thought.

plans.reason: The g2 bishop on the long diagonal is the key piece.
